finding: The new IOU anchors on the 0005 contract, but that contract does not name the symbol or the held-map work.
why: The wiring rule needs an anchor that names the symbol the consumer will use, and the 0005 contract has no text for `data-afkv2-element`, `_element_ids`, a held map, node id uniqueness or the round check, so its Acceptance and Verification rows do not require the work that D-43 passes to it.
fix: Have the orchestrator add to the 0005 contract one Acceptance bullet and one Verification row that name `engine._element_ids` and maps held in a card or a table cell, and change the engine.py Scope note; the executor of 0004 cannot edit that contract.
evidence: User CLAUDE.md: 'declare an IOU in the repo's `.claude/wiring-ious.md`, anchored to a plan step / ticket / contract naming *your* symbol the consumer will call'. New line: '-> anchor: contract "docs/afk/afkv2/plan-s1/0005-notes-ingest-live-test.md" (PRD AC-035, a note on every map node), orchestrator ruling recorded as D-43: `engine._element_ids` must register these nodes'. Separate check by grep of the 0005 contract and PLAN.md, pattern `_element_ids|data-afkv2-element|D-43|held`: 0 hits. A second grep, pattern `card|table cell|map node|engine.py`, finds line 24 'afkv2/engine/engine.py   # register the ingest verb' and generic note bullets at lines 36 and 37, and no bullet on held maps, duplicate ids or rounds. Limit: DECISIONS.md D-43 does record the ruling and an executor reads that ledger, so the gap is not lost, but no contract row makes it a gate.

criterion: Boundary values: a forward arrow and a taller box in the rank of its source
finding: A forward arrow still passes behind a box: the lane check reads only the ranks between the two ends, so a taller box in the source rank hides the curve and the picture shows a false connection.
why: D-42 supersedes the D-39 gap 'for forward arrows', but line 142 skips every arrow between adjacent ranks and line 145 reads only ranks low+1 to high-1. In direction down, nodes s, l (label 'long label text ' x 12), x, y with edges s->y and l->x give s->y the path 'M112 60 C112 178 308 178 308 296', and box l is left 220, top 24, width 176, height 216. The curve goes into the left side of l near y=187 and comes out of the bottom of l near x=270, so a reader sees s->l and l->y. PRD CMP-5 requires the graph to draw its arrows.
fix: Include the boxes of the source rank that extend past the source box in the way-check, for all forward arrows, and start the arrow in the gap (straight to first_gap, as the lane branch does); add a test in both directions with a tall sibling.
evidence: `if index in back or high - low < 2:` and `between = [span for rank in range(low + 1, high) for span in spans[rank]]`. Separate probe: sampled each path in 201 points against each box. 27.9% of the s->y points are inside box l. Direction right with a held component: s->z 'M200 42 C272 42 272 154 344 154' against held box left 24, top 80, width 264, height 136 has 24.9% inside (the box ends at x=288, the source ends at x=200). A fuzz of 1500 random graphs had 9 hidden forward arrows on 8 graphs, and in all 9 the box is in the source rank and the path is a curve. Trigger in direction down: the sibling is more than 56px taller (by the arithmetic of `middle`, not measured at the limit). Box z-index 2 over svg z-index 1 is from diagram.css; the positions are computed, not seen in a browser.

finding: The long-label canvas test uses only a forward arrow, and a long label on a self arrow in the down direction leaves the canvas at the top.
why: D-42 states for all labels that no label left the canvas, and PRD AC-042 lists long text and no cut-off content, but `low = main - main_size // 2` in diagram_boxes.py has no floor on the main axis, so a label of 125 or more characters on a self arrow of a first-rank node gets a negative box top; the test never reaches this path.
fix: Add a self-arrow and a back-arrow case to this test (its `top >= 0` then fails), and floor or shift `low` in `_arrows`.
evidence: Test line: `"edges": [{"from": "a", "to": "b", "label": "a long label " * 20}]`. In-memory render, direction down, one node a, edge a to a, same label: canvas 384x134, label box by the test's own label_boxes formula (204, -46, 176, 176). Threshold: 125 chars gives box top -6. A fuzz of 6000 graphs gave 93 hits, all with back or self arrows. Mutant `main_end` growth removed also survives all 113 tests. Browser clipping is not verified; the CSS is `transform: translate(-50%, -50%)` on an absolute element.

finding: Each lane stays apart from every earlier lane, also when the 2 arrows share no rank, so render time grows by about the cube of the arrow count and the canvas grows with it.
why: `taken` holds all earlier lanes, so `reach` and the `clear` check both grow with the lane count, and a chain with a skip arrow at each step takes 28 seconds at 800 nodes and gets a canvas 6452px tall, while its row of boxes needs only about 84px with lanes that reuse a free position.
fix: Compare a lane only with earlier lanes whose rank range overlaps this arrow's rank range.
evidence: `lanes[index] = _free_lane(between, near, set(lanes.values()))`; `reach = LANE_GAP * (2 * len(taken) + 1)`. Own timing with registry.render_component on one machine, nodes 0..n-1, edges i->i+1 and i->i+2: n=100 0.05s height 852; n=200 0.34s height 1652; n=400 2.97s height 3252; n=800 27.93s height 6452. The class docstring on `_Taken` says 'so a long chain stays cheap', and test_a_long_chain_draws_without_a_recursion_failure uses 3000 nodes with no skip arrow. The 84px figure is inferred from the layout constants and not measured. Pages of this size are not verified as a real use; PRD AC-042 asks only for 'big diagrams'.

criterion: Acceptance: A graph draws nodes and arrows, including grouped boxes for module structure (PRD CMP-5)
finding: A back arrow runs behind the next box in its stack, so it can look as if it starts at that box; one box below is enough, not only the 'tall stack' that D-42 records.
why: The bullet requires the graph to draw its arrows, and on edges a->b, a->c, b->a the dashed b->a arc leaves b, goes behind c, and comes out at the left side of c, so the picture reads as c->a; D-42 is this slice's own record and not a ruling on the bullet, and its words understate the gap, because the arc goes 42px past the source box (BACK_ARC 56 at 3/4) and the next box starts at CROSS_GAP 20.
fix: Route a back arrow with a box in its way through a free lane, as _lanes does for a forward arrow, or else start and end it on a box side that is clear; add a test with the fan-out and retry shape that asserts the path crosses no box.
evidence: Line 258: curve = f"M{at(from_main, from_cross)} C{at(from_main, far)} {at(tip_main, far)} {at(tip_main, end)}". D-42: 'Still a known gap: a back arrow can pass behind a box in a tall stack'. Separate probe with registry.render_component, sampling each path against the box rectangles. Direction right, nodes a,b,c: boxes (24,24,176,36) (264,24,176,36) (264,80,176,36), path 'b a' M364 60 C364 116 100 116 100 68, 28% of the samples are behind box c. Direction down: 18% behind c. Three boxes per rank, direction right: 60% hidden. 1500 random graphs: of 1785 back arrows, 915 are more than 2% hidden, 419 more than 25%, 58 more than 50%, 0 more than 90%. A grep of test_diagram_components.py for 'back arrow' and 'tall stack' has no hits. Coordinates are observed; the page was not opened in a browser for this finding (visual result unverified).

criterion: Boundary values: the label height estimate assumes full lines and one glyph width
finding: A label with many long words or with wide glyphs is taller than the estimate, so labels land on labels and on boxes and go past the canvas, which the remediation says no longer happens.
why: `ceil(length / (label_width - LABEL_PAD))` counts characters as if each line fills up, but the text wraps at spaces, and EDGE_CHAR of 7 is too small for a wide glyph (about 12px by the measured rects, inferred from the wrap). The collision check and the canvas size then use a false height. Ordinary prose and identifiers pass (measured), so this needs words of about 14 to 17 characters in a row or a full-width script. This breaks PRD AC-042 and the D-42 result 'no label touched a box or a label or left the canvas'.
fix: Count lines word by word in `_label_size` and in `_gap`, and count a wide glyph (unicodedata.east_asian_width) at about 12px; add both inputs to the tests.
evidence: `height = EDGE_LINE * ceil(length / (layout.label_width - LABEL_PAD))`. Headless Edge: direction right, a->b with 'abcdefghijklmn ' x 12: rect top -28, bottom 164, canvas height 136. Direction right, a->b and a->c with 'abcdefghijklmn ' x 6: rects 62..90 overlap by 28px, first top -6. Direction down, a->b with 'abcdefghijklmnop qrstuvwxyzabcdef ' x 6: rect 48..240 covers box a (ends 60) and box b (starts 228). Direction right, a->b and a->c with 30 CJK characters each: rects 18..66 and 54..102 overlap by 12px. Labels with a higher z-index and an opaque background hide what they cover. test helper label_boxes computes the same formula, so the tests cannot see this (read, not mutated).

criterion: Boundary values: a label placed over a group title
finding: In direction right, an arrow label can land on a group title and hide its text, because the taken set holds boxes only.
why: _Taken starts from layout.places, and layout.frames is not in it. In direction right the head of a band is above its boxes and across the gaps, and no room is kept for a label there. An arrow from an upper band into a group that spans 2 ranks has its label near that head, and the label has an opaque background and a higher z-index. This breaks PRD AC-042 'no content is hidden or cut off'.
fix: Add to `taken` the head strip of each frame (frame left, frame top, frame width, head height) when a frame is drawn, in main and cross terms.
evidence: `taken = _Taken((place.main, place.cross, place.main_size, place.cross_size) for place in layout.places.values())`. Headless Edge: direction right, group g titled with 82 characters, nodes a, p (g), q (g), edges p->q and a->q with a 3-line label: title line left 21, top 93, right 469, bottom 109; label left 204, top 92, right 372, bottom 140, so the label covers 168px of the title line. With a 2-line label, the overlap is 9px in height. Reach: the title text must pass x=204, about 30 characters at .78rem (inferred from 448px for 82 characters).

finding: The fix keeps a label on the canvas on the cross axis only: on the main axis, a long label on a self-loop in direction down starts above the canvas.
why: `rect_cross` is clamped with `max(LABEL_GAP, ...)` but `low` has no clamp, and a self-loop has a small main centre, so a label of more than 120 characters has a negative top edge and scrolling cannot reach that text, which is the failure that review finding r-004 reported against PRD AC-042 'no content is hidden or cut off'.
fix: Clamp the main axis too: shift `main` so that `low >= LABEL_GAP`, and add a case for a self-loop with a long label in direction down to the canvas test.
evidence: `low = main - main_size // 2` beside `max(LABEL_GAP, cross - cross_size // 2)`. Own probe through registry.validate and registry.render_component, direction down, one node, edge a->a: validate gives [] and the label is at `top:42px` for each length. Height from `_label_size`: 150 characters give 112px, so the top edge is -14px; 300 characters give 208px, so the top edge is -62px; canvas height 150. The forward-arrow test test_a_long_arrow_label_stays_on_the_canvas has no back arrow or self-loop. The label height is the code's estimate; the page was not opened in a browser (visual result unverified).

finding: `turns` drops the minus sign, so the `0 <= x` and `0 <= y` half of the canvas assertion can never fail.
why: A negative lane coordinate is read as a positive one, so the check that claims to keep corners on the canvas cannot see the failure it names, and `crosses` also gets a mirrored point.
evidence: `numbers = [int(number) for number in re.findall(r"\d+", curve)]` (line 397) feeds `assert all(0 <= x <= width and 0 <= y <= height for x, y in corners)` (line 439). `re.findall(r"\d+", "M-8 0")` gives ['8', '0']. In-memory mutant removing `at >= LANE_CLEAR` from `_free_lane` survives all 113 tests.

finding: Every lane test skips exactly one rank that holds one box, so a box in a later skipped rank is not tested.
why: `_lanes` collects spans over `range(low + 1, high)`, and a mutant that reads only the first skipped rank passes all tests but draws a lane through a box.
fix: Add a case that skips 2 ranks with a box in the second skipped rank only, off the line of the first skipped rank's box, and a case with a stack of 2 boxes in the skipped rank.
evidence: `skip_graph` docstring: "Node order a, c, b, with one arrow from a to b that skips c." In-memory mutant `for rank in range(low + 1, low + 2)`: 113 passed; a seeded fuzz of 2500 forward-only graphs under this mutant gave `crosses` hits on 5 graphs, and 0 on the unmodified code.

finding: No test pins the route of a lane arrow, so a diagonal first leg, the farthest lane and a label away from its lane all pass.
why: D-42 specifies "the nearest free lane through straight segments" and the contract's unit tier promises render snapshots, but the tests only assert the end points and no crossing of the one box.
fix: Assert the exact path for one case, for example `M200 42 L232 42 L232 16 L472 16 L472 42 L496 42` for direction right, or assert every segment is axis-aligned and the lane is the nearest one.
evidence: `corners = turns(edge_paths(html)["a b"])`. In-memory mutants, 113 passed each: `(first_gap, from_cross), (first_gap, lane),` reduced to `(first_gap, lane),`; `key=lambda at: (-abs(at - near), at)`; lane label at `(first_gap, from_cross)`. Contract: "render snapshots; prop refusals". `grep snapshot|approv` on the test file gave no hit.

finding: The lane test stops at 2 parallel arrows and proves only that 2 lanes differ, so lane reach, lane spacing and canvas growth for lanes are not tested.
why: A mutant with a fixed reach raises ValueError from `min()` on real graphs and a mutant that drops lanes from `cross_end` puts a lane off the canvas, and both pass all tests because the fixture has too few arrows to need either line.
fix: Parametrize 6 parallel arrows and assert 6 routes, pairwise lane distance of at least 8, and every corner on the canvas (today's output has lanes 16, 68, 8, 76, 84, 92 on a canvas of height 116).
evidence: `assert len(routes) == 2 and routes[0][2] != routes[1][2]`. In-memory mutants that survive all 113 tests: `reach = LANE_GAP` (ValueError on 7 of 2500 fuzz graphs), `cross_end = cross - BAND_GAP + START`, and `abs(at - lane) < 1`. The canvas effect of the second mutant at 6 arrows is derived by reading (height falls to 84, lane 92 is outside), not run.

finding: The label-collision tests do not exercise the `_Taken` cell lookup or its sort order, because no fixture has labels of different sizes on one arrow gap.
why: Three mutants of `_Taken`, added in this remediation to keep labels apart, pass all tests but make labels overlap on small graphs, so "never land on each other" is not proved for them.
fix: Add parameter cases with mixed sizes: two nodes, direction right, labels `"e " * 4` and `"e " * 12` in both orders; direction down, labels `"e " * 12`, `"e " * 60`, `"e " * 4`.
evidence: Parameter sets at line 462 use equal-size labels per case. In-memory mutants, 113 passed each, then label-label overlaps in a 2500-graph fuzz: `key=lambda other: -other[1]` 128 graphs, `cells = range(main // LABEL_CELL, main // LABEL_CELL + 1)` 55 graphs, `for cell in (rect[0] // LABEL_CELL,):` 57 graphs. The unmodified code gave 0, and the smallest fixtures above came from that search.

criterion: Acceptance: A graph draws nodes and arrows, including grouped boxes for module structure (PRD CMP-5)
finding: A forward arrow from a short box can still pass behind a taller box of its own rank, but D-42 says the gap is closed for forward arrows.
why: _lanes looks only at ranks strictly between the two ends and skips an arrow of one rank, so the curve from a short box crosses the lower part of a taller neighbour; both ends stay visible, so the harm is small, but the D-42 record and the 15:16 journal line 'arrows no longer hide behind a box' claim more than the code does.
fix: Start the curve at the gap of the source rank (run straight to first_gap first), or else narrow the D-42 'Supersedes' text to arrows that skip a rank.
evidence: Probe, direction down, nodes a (short), t (5 lines), z, r, edges a->z, t->r, a->r: boxes (24,24,176,36) (220,24,176,116) (24,204,176,36) (220,204,176,36), path 'a r' M112 60 C112 128 308 128 308 196, 8% of the samples are behind box t. 1500 random graphs: 64 of 10070 forward arrows are more than 2% hidden, the worst 21%, none more than 25%. D-42: 'Supersedes: D-39 ... for forward arrows and all labels'. Lines 142 and 145: 'if index in back or high - low < 2: continue', 'between = [span for rank in range(low + 1, high) ...'.

finding: Possible conditional test logic: an `if direction` branch selects the asserts inside one test body.
why: The checklist asks to split or parameterize `if` steering asserts; a failure here does not show which expected shape was used without reading the branch.
fix: Move the expected first and last corners into the `parametrize` values, or read them through a small helper for each direction.
evidence: `if direction == "right":` followed by `assert corners[0] == (source[0] + source[2], source[1] + source[3] // 2)`.

finding: Possible weak test: the max-content test greps the CSS source, and its pattern also matches `max-width: max-content`.
why: It proves one line of text exists and not that a label keeps its width at the canvas edge, and the pattern has no boundary before `width`, so a wrong property passes.
fix: Anchor the pattern with `[{;\s]width: max-content;`, and name the live browser test of AC-042 as the real proof in a test comment or the plan.
